title: Micro publish starter kit and technical acceptance
content:
Purpose: quick, repeatable starter kit for publishing a small partner tile (trial or single-SKU) to a cloud marketplace. Not a replacement for full Marketplace Runbook — this is intentionally compact and ops-friendly for fast pilots.

Audience: partner solutions/product managers, GTM engineers, devrel and ops who need a minimal checklist + copy templates + technical acceptance tests to ship a tile in a single sprint.

Status: draft — checklist tuned for 48–72 hour preflight window.

-- Quick summary (TL;DR) --
- Goal: get a validated, telemetry-backed tile live in marketplace staging in 48 hours, production within 7 calendar days.
- Scope: basic tile with 1 SKU (trial or paid), minimal auth (API key or oauth), simple onboarding doc, monitoring hooks.
- Must-haves before submit: working billing SKU mapping, privacy blurb, basic SSO or API contract sample, e2e smoke tests, tile copy (30–60 words) and 3 bullets.

-- Preflight checklist (compact) --
1) Copy and assets
   - Tile name (clear, searchable) — avoid generic "AI" only names. Provide 30–60 char short title.
   - One-line summary (<= 140 chars).
   - 3 bullets (benefits, not features). Prioritize action verbs.
   - Hero image (PNG 1200x628 or vendor size, alt text present).
   - Link to Quickstart (public docs or transient staging link).

2) Billing & SKUs
   - Confirm marketplace SKU id and internal billing mapping.
   - Fallback SKU: predefine a fallback for trial-to-paid transition.
   - Pricing tier mapping doc link and contact person for finance approvals.

3) Technical contracts & onboarding
   - API contract sample (curl + JSON example) in docs.
   - Auth options documented (API key or OAuth 2.0 with redirect URL) and tested in staging.
   - Entitlement mapping: how marketplace entitlement maps to internal tenant ID.

4) Security & compliance light checks
   - Privacy blurb (one short paragraph) — what data is stored, any PII handling.
   - KMS note: which KMS is used for secrets in private deployments (if applicable).
   - Minimal pen-test note: no external endpoints exposing raw user data; if there are, flag for security review.

5) Observability & telemetry
   - Add a market-specific event: marketplace_provisioned, marketplace_trial_started, marketplace_activated.
   - Quick logs: correlate marketplace_order_id -> internal_account_id in traces.
   - Dashboard: 7-day funnel (provisions -> first request -> active).

6) E2E smoke tests (CLI-friendly)
   - Provision flow: simulate purchase/provisioning with marketplace test buyer account. Verify tenant created and entitlement set.
   - Login or API request using entitlement headers. Expect 200 + sample payload.
   - Billing event sync: confirm marketplace webhook received and internal billing record created.

7) UX fallbacks and error messages
   - Onboarding failure message clear to end-user: "Provisioning delayed — we will retry and notify you by email".
   - If entitlements cannot be mapped, auto-create escrow tenant and notify ops.

8) Rollout & rollback plan
   - Canary rule: 5% shard for first 24 hours. Manual promotion thereafter.
   - Rollback: disable SKU mapping and deprovision new entitlements; maintain read-only API for existing customers.

-- Minimal copy templates (editable) --
Tile short title: "Redwood Inference — Hosted LLM Inference"
30–60 char summary (example): "Low-latency, cost-aware hosted inference for production LLMs."
3 bullets (examples):
 - "Fast, predictable inference — enterprise SLAs and latency SLOs."
 - "Cost controls — batching, caching, and quantization recommendations."
 - "Deploy where you need it — hosted, dedicated, or private (VPC)."

Micro-snippets for trial CTA: "Start free trial — deploy a demo model in minutes"
Onboarding step microcopy: "Confirm billing to finalize provisioning; you’ll receive access credentials by email."

-- Technical acceptance tests (detailed steps) --
A) Provision simulation (automated)
   - Step 1: Use marketplace test webhook to POST {order_id, sku, customer_email} to /marketplace/webhook/test.
   - Step 2: Consumer service must create internal tenant with tag marketplace:test and return 202.
   - Step 3: Check event downstream: marketplace_provisioned logged with both order_id and tenant_id.

B) API smoke request
   - Use API_KEY_TEST token, call /v1/generate with prompt "hello world" and expect 200 + well-formed response within 2s p50.

C) Billing reconciliation (manual for pilot)
   - Verify marketplace reports match internal billing for test period; create a finance ticket if mismatch > 1%.

D) Security checklist (ops)
   - Ensure no secret is returned in any API response.
   - Confirm CSP headers and TLS 1.2+ enforced.
   - Confirm webhook endpoint validates marketplace signature header.

-- Deployment notes (ops-runbook fragments) --
- Staging namespace: marketplace-staging-<partner-short>. Use ephemeral DB schema.
- Shared secrets: store in KMS path projects/marketplace/<partner>. Use short TTL tokens for provisioning.
- CI smoke: add marketplace-staging e2e to release pipeline with a toggle.

-- Telemetry and post-launch checklist (first 72h) --
- Monitor: provisioning failures (>= 1% spike), API 5xx rate, latency p95 changes > 30%.
- Verify onboarding email delivered rates and token expirations.
- Schedule a 24-hour sync with partner and Platform Ops after go-live.

-- Mini UX test ideas (cheap, fast) --
- A/B tile subtitle: emphasize "SLA" vs "Cost-savings"; measure CTR in marketplace analytics for 72 hours.
- Swap hero image variant with user avatar vs abstract compute graphic. Track clicks to quickstart.

-- Template Jira tickets (examples to copy/paste) --
- MKP-XXXXX: Onboard partner <partner> to marketplace staging — include links to SKU, quickstart, tile copy, and owner.
- MKP-XXXXX: Acceptance test: provision simulation, API smoke, billing reconciliation.

-- Known open questions / decisions to make --
- Do we allow partner-controlled provisioning webhooks for pilot or insist on intermediary staging queue? (ops prefers queue).
- If partner requests private data storage in tenant, escalate to security/compliance — this will likely push to Private product offering.

-- Contacts & escalation matrix --
- GTM owner: Evelyn Zhou (evelyn.z@redwood.com)
- Engineering on-call (marketplace): Ben Carter (pager)
- Finance billing lead: Aisha Ramirez
- Security reviewer: Liam O'Neill

-- Notes to self (informal) --
- Keep copy punchy: marketplace text is scanned quickly; prioritize one measurable benefit.
- For pilots, accept manual finance reconciliation but log it clearly.
- Add a short README for partner with exact steps and sample curl commands (makes life easier for partner PMs).

-- Appendix: small set of sample curl commands --
1) Provision webhook (example):
curl -X POST https://staging.redwood.com/marketplace/webhook/test \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"order_id":"test-123","sku":"redwood-llm-trial","email":"pilot+test@example.com"}'

2) API smoke call (example):
curl -X POST https://staging.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer API_KEY_TEST' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello world","max_tokens":16}'

-- End --

Quick note: keep this doc minimal and copyable. If a partner asks for more, point them to the full marketplace runbook (Confluence link in linked artifacts).

Action items (first pass):
- [ ] Finalize tile copy with partner comms (owner: Evelyn)
- [ ] Confirm SKU mapping with finance (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Wire up webhook test harness in staging (owner: Ben)
